name: Rebalance the Balancing Portfolio to target exposures (daily review)
summary: Every trading day the Balancing Portfolio Management team checks whether the whole fund still has the exposures it is meant to have once all active programs are counted, and trades a completion portfolio of public securities to close the gaps. The morning starts with an overnight exposure aggregation that analysts must check for data gaps, then associates measure drift against targets and ranges, a senior associate decides whether and how far to trade, and trade lists pass a liquidity check, a four-eyes review and, for large moves, director or group head approval before going to the central trading desk. Elapsed time is driven by the overnight batch, data fixes, approvals and execution through the session; errors come mostly from data gaps, private-asset proxies and re-keying spreadsheets into the order system. Large private fundings and market shocks force unplanned rebalancing.

baseline.org_archetype: A national pension fund manager of about C$540 billion that runs a public-market Balancing Portfolio of about C$228 billion to complete the exposures of its active programs.
baseline.notes: Describes the Toronto team after Total Fund Management was formed in September 2020 by combining Total Portfolio Management and Balancing & Collateral. Tooling is spreadsheet-heavy with a data platform, a risk platform and an order management system.

trigger: The daily fund valuation and positions are available after the overnight batch, together with the liquidity forecast and any remediation plan from Risk.
end_state: Either rebalancing trades are executed, reconciled and the daily log signed off, or a no-trade decision is recorded with the exposure summary.

volume.seasonality: One review per trading day. Workload is heavier in volatile markets (for example March 2020), around quarterly futures rolls, at large private closings and at fiscal year end.

evidence.note: Daily process stated in the F2021 report; trading days per month from the calendar.

steps.name: Aggregate overnight exposures
steps.description: After the daily fund valuation lands, a scheduled job in the enterprise data platform combines active program and Balancing Portfolio positions and maps them to factor, currency, region and credit exposures for the base and additional plan accounts and the Core Pool. Private holdings are mapped through proxies. The output is a set of exposure tables and a dashboard for the morning review.
inputs: daily net asset value and positions

error.defect_description: A late price feed, a missing position, a failed proxy mapping for a private holding or a stale FX rate leaves exposures misstated.

evidence.note: The F2021 report says each day the balancing process starts with a daily aggregation of risk, factor, currency and geographic exposures. Batch timing is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check exposure data quality
steps.description: The analyst opens the exposure dashboard and checks that all portfolios loaded, compares totals with the prior day and the daily valuation, and looks for large unexplained moves, stale prices and private holdings without a current proxy. Anything that does not tie out is logged for a fix before the numbers are used.

error.defect_description: A real data gap is accepted as a market move.

control.basis: Data and user-developed application controls maintained by Finance, Analytics and Risk and Technology and Data under the Integrated Risk Framework

evidence.note: The F2021 report describes formal protocols for managing data, models and user-developed applications. Check content, times and the 12% issue rate are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Chase data fixes and rerun exposures
steps.description: The analyst messages the pricing and data operations team or the risk technology support desk with the missing item, waits for a corrected price, position or mapping, and asks for the exposure job to be rerun. If a fix cannot come in time, the analyst applies a documented manual adjustment and flags it in the summary.
outputs: corrected exposure report or manual adjustment

error.defect_description: A manual adjustment is entered with the wrong sign or left in place the next day.

evidence.note: Common practice when a daily batch depends on upstream pricing and reference data. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large in-house balancing team.

steps.name: Gather known cash flows and planned trades
steps.description: The analyst pulls the day's liquidity forecast, private closings and capital calls due in the next few days from the deal pipeline, plan transfer dates and any large trades active programs have flagged. These flows change exposures before markets move and decide whether cash must be raised or invested.

error.defect_description: A large private funding is missed or dated wrongly, so the trade list leaves cash short or exposure off target.

evidence.note: TFM must keep liquidity to cover plan net outflows, contractual obligations and committed investments (F2021). Steps and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Compare exposures with targets and ranges
steps.description: The associate lines up the validated exposures and expected flows against current-year target exposures, the equity/debt risk target and the tolerance ranges for factors, currency, regions and credit. The spreadsheet shows the drift in each bucket in dollars and percentage points and the estimated cost to correct it.

error.defect_description: A bucket is mapped to the wrong target or a currency drift is read in the wrong direction.

evidence.note: Exposures are compared with intended Core Pool allocations and total risk target; trades follow when they have diverged too far. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Decide whether and how far to rebalance
steps.description: The senior associate reviews the drift analysis and decides whether today's drift and flows justify trading, how much of the gap to close and whether to spread trades over several days. The call weighs tracking against targets with transaction costs, market liquidity and what active programs are about to do.

error.defect_description: A trade is skipped or oversized because a flow or a cost estimate was misjudged.

next.condition: an exposure is outside a management threshold

evidence.note: The balancing group determines when, to what extent and by what means rebalancing is required (F2021); peers trade off band width against costs (NBIM). Branch shares are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Choose instruments and timing
steps.description: The senior associate chooses how to deliver the change: equity index or bond futures, total return swaps, ETFs or cash securities in the Balancing Portfolio blocks, and whether to trade at the open, through the day or at the close. The choice considers financing cost, margin, leverage use and how the trade affects the liquidity coverage ratio.

error.defect_description: A costlier instrument is chosen or a swap is used where no financing line is available.

next.condition: large or less liquid trade, desk input needed

evidence.note: Distinct asset blocks are kept to rebalance factor exposures cost-effectively (F2021); derivatives are used to achieve intended exposures (Investment Statement); futures overlays (Russell); completion portfolio offsets active program exposures (Thinking Ahead Institute). Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Give market colour and cost estimate
steps.description: A trader on the central desk looks at market depth, futures roll calendars and recent volumes and replies with an estimated cost and a suggested execution approach, for example splitting a large futures order over two sessions or using an index swap with a dealer.

evidence.note: FCT oversees global trading and execution of public assets for all teams and the Balancing Portfolio and works with TFM on liquidity, financing and execution trade-offs. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Build the trade list and post-trade exposures
steps.description: The associate turns the plan into a trade list in the rebalancing spreadsheet: instrument, side, contract count or notional, account and pool, with currency legs. The sheet recalculates exposures, leverage and estimated margin after the trades so the reviewer can see the result.

error.defect_description: Wrong contract multiplier, sign, account or currency on a line.

evidence.note: Spreadsheet-based trade list building was common at large asset owners in 2019 to 2022. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large in-house balancing team.

steps.name: Confirm cash, margin and collateral capacity
steps.description: The liquidity and collateral principal checks the draft list against the day's cash position, the liquidity forecast, initial margin needed for new futures and swap financing lines, and the collateral available. If the list would push the liquidity coverage ratio toward its floor or needs collateral that is not free, it goes back for resizing or a funding action.

control.basis: Board-approved liquidity risk limit and 10-day liquidity coverage ratio minimum of 1.0x in the Risk Policy

evidence.note: Liquidity must meet collateral and margin requirements and permit changes in composition; 10-day LCR limit 1.0x. Branch share and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Review the trade list
steps.description: A principal who did not build the list checks each line against the decision, the target ranges and the post-trade exposures, and confirms sizes are within the team's delegated trading authority. Errors or unclear rationale send the list back to the associate.

control.basis: Four-eyes review of trade lists before release under TFM delegated trading authorities

evidence.note: Independent review is standard trading control practice; delegated limits are not published. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large in-house balancing team.

steps.name: Approve large or non-routine rebalancing
steps.description: A TFM director reviews rebalancing that exceeds the principal's delegated size, moves several exposures at once or follows a large private funding. The director checks the rationale, cost estimate and timing and approves by email or sends the list back.

control.basis: Delegated investment and trading authorities under the Investment Statement and Investment Strategy and Risk Committee delegations

evidence.note: Management acts within delegated authorities and Board limits; thresholds are not published. Shares and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Approve very large rebalancing and brief the CIO
steps.description: The TFM group head reviews a very large or unusual rebalancing, such as moving several billion dollars of equity exposure after a market shock, approves it and briefs the Chief Investment Officer, who may ask for the trade to be phased.

control.basis: Delegated authority escalation for large total fund exposure changes

evidence.note: Escalation tier assumed from the Analyst to Managing Director ladder. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large in-house balancing team.

steps.name: Send the credit leg to Public Credit
steps.description: When the change includes credit exposure, the associate sends the credit amount, direction and timing to the Public Credit team, which manages the balancing credit portfolio and picks the bonds, credit ETFs or index products itself.

error.defect_description: Amount sent in the wrong currency or account.

evidence.note: Public Credit manages the balancing credit portfolio to keep total fund credit exposure at the desired level. Share and time are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Stage orders in the order management system
steps.description: The associate enters or uploads the approved lines into the order management system, choosing account, instrument, side, quantity and instructions for the desk. This re-keys what is already in the spreadsheet, so quantities and accounts are checked again on screen.

error.defect_description: Keying error in side, quantity or account.

evidence.note: Re-keying or uploading from spreadsheets into the order system is common. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large in-house balancing team.

steps.name: Run pre-trade compliance checks
steps.description: The order management system tests each staged order against coded rules such as the restricted list, account and mandate permissions, position and concentration limits and fat finger size checks. Passing orders release to the desk blotter; breaches raise an alert.

control.basis: Pre-trade compliance rules coded in the order management system (restricted list, mandate and size limits)

evidence.note: Pre-trade checks and hard or soft blocks in trading systems. Alert rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Resolve a compliance alert
steps.description: The senior associate reads the alert, decides whether the order is wrong or the rule is too tight for a futures position, and either amends the order or asks Compliance for a documented override. Overrides are logged with a reason.

control.basis: Compliance approval of soft-block overrides with a logged reason

evidence.note: Soft blocks can be overridden; firms set when supervisory approval applies. Shares and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Accept orders and agree the execution approach
steps.description: A trader on the central desk picks up the released orders, checks them against any cost advice given earlier and confirms timing with the associate, for example working futures through the afternoon and finishing at the close. Execution then runs in the trade execution process.

evidence.note: FCT executes trades for the Balancing Portfolio. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Monitor fills and intraday exposures
steps.description: Through the trading day the associate watches fills in the order system and the intraday exposure view. If markets move sharply or orders fill only partly, the associate flags it to the senior associate and prepares top-up or reduced lines.

next.condition: market move or partial fill needs new lines

evidence.note: The F2021 report notes rebalancing trades executed in volatile markets. Wait reflects execution through the session; shares are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Reconcile executions and update post-trade exposures
steps.description: After the close the associate ties executed quantities and prices to the trade list, records any unfilled residual for tomorrow and refreshes the post-trade exposure and leverage figures with actual fills.

error.defect_description: A residual is not carried forward.

evidence.note: End-of-day tie-out of executions against intended trades is common practice. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large in-house balancing team.

steps.name: Publish the daily exposure and rebalancing summary
steps.description: The associate sends TFM leadership, the liquidity team and Risk a short summary of exposures against targets, trades done and their rationale, margin impact and residuals, and saves it with the trade list in the team folder.

evidence.note: Daily summaries to stakeholders are common practice. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large in-house balancing team.

steps.name: Sign off the daily balancing log
steps.description: A principal reads the summary and trade record, confirms the rationale is recorded and the residuals are owned, and signs off the log, which second and third line reviewers can later sample.

control.basis: Documented rationale for portfolio decisions available to Risk, internal audit and the special examiner

evidence.note: Record-keeping control assumed from the three lines of defence model described in the F2022 report. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large in-house balancing team.

steps.name: Escalate an exposure outside threshold and agree remediation
steps.description: When an exposure or the leverage or liquidity measure is outside a management-level threshold, or Risk has sent a remediation plan, a TFM director reviews the cause with Risk, agrees how fast to bring it back and records the plan before trades are built.

control.basis: Integrated Risk Policy: management-level limits and thresholds and breach escalation procedures

evidence.note: Breach treatment and escalation are set in the Risk Policy; Risk independently monitors compliance. Frequency and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Record a no-trade decision and circulate the exposure summary
steps.description: On days when exposures are inside their ranges and no large flows are due, the associate records the no-trade decision with the drift figures and sends the short exposure summary to TFM leadership and the liquidity team.

evidence.note: Share of no-trade days is the author's estimate: flows from private programs and plan transfers mean most days need some trading. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large in-house balancing team.

exceptions.name: Exposure data gap or late batch
exceptions.description: A missing price, position or private-asset proxy forces a fix and rerun before the review can proceed, delaying trading decisions into late morning.

exceptions.name: Large private funding or market shock
exceptions.description: A multi-billion closing, capital call cluster or sharp equity move forces an unplanned rebalancing that needs desk input and director or group head approval and may be phased over several days.

exceptions.name: Exposure outside a management threshold
exceptions.description: An exposure, leverage or liquidity measure sits outside a threshold or Risk sends a remediation plan; a director agrees the remediation with Risk before trades are built.

exceptions.name: Pre-trade compliance alert
exceptions.description: An order trips a restricted-list, mandate or size rule and must be amended or overridden with Compliance approval.

exceptions.name: Partial fills or intraday market move
exceptions.description: Orders do not complete or markets move enough that the list is rebuilt with top-up or reduced lines the same day.

exceptions.name: Quarterly futures roll
exceptions.description: In roll weeks expiring equity and bond futures must be rolled to the next contract, adding roll lines to the trade list and desk coordination.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the daily valuation becoming available to the signed-off balancing log
benchmarks.population: Daily balancing reviews at a large in-house pension fund manager

evidence.note: The process is daily and starts with the overnight aggregation (F2021); the author estimates the valuation and exposure data are ready between about 01:00 and 03:00 and the log is signed off between about 17:00 and 19:00, with large or disrupted days running into the evening.
Balancing Portfolio grew from C$176 billion in F2018 to C$228 billion in F2022.

evidence.note: 64.6% active, 35.4% Balancing Portfolios.

benchmarks.unit: equity share of equivalent two-asset portfolio

evidence.note: Note 7.2 table of key investment risk governance measures.

benchmarks.unit: percentage points of equity share before rebalancing is triggered (proposal to narrow to about 2)

evidence.note: Peer fund rule; not this organisation.

pain_points.description: Exposure numbers depend on an overnight chain of pricing, positions and private-asset proxies; a late or missing input holds up the morning review and manual adjustments can linger.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice; the F2021 report describes a multi-year initiative to improve public markets trading and collateral technology and data quality.

pain_points.description: Trade lists are built in spreadsheets and re-keyed or uploaded into the order management system, so the same quantities are checked twice and keying errors still slip through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common 2019 to 2022 tooling.

pain_points.description: Large or non-routine rebalancing waits for director or group head availability during market hours, which can push execution into the next session.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Private fundings and capital calls arrive with uncertain timing, so the team must hold buffers or trade at short notice to keep exposures and cash on target.

evidence.note: TFM keeps liquidity for committed investments and plan outflows; F2021 notes rebalancing in volatile markets.

assumptions: The unit of work is one trading day's review; a large rebalancing phased over several days appears as several daily cases.

About 72% of trading days lead to some trades because private program flows, plan transfers and market drift change exposures most days; 25% end with no trade and 3% start with an exposure outside a management threshold. These shares are estimates.
Delegated trading sizes for principal, director and group head approval are not published; the branch shares (22% of trading days to a director, of which 12% to the group head) are estimates.

Credit adjustments are handed to Public Credit, which executes them in its own process; equity, rates, FX and derivative orders go to the central trading desk. Execution time is shown only as the wait before the associate's monitoring step.

fte_on_process covers only this daily cycle. The 18-person balancing team also designs Balancing Portfolio blocks, manages Core and Supplementary Pool weights, runs currency management and research, so stated FTE is about twice the FTE implied by hands-on time.
Loaded hourly costs come from the organisation file. They are far above Job Bank market medians because they include large incentive pay, so labour cost per case is high relative to effort.

The Investment Statement cited is the April 2025 version served at the 2020 address; its rebalancing, liquidity and limit provisions match the F2021 and F2022 annual report descriptions for the reference period.
Exposure aggregation is placed in the enterprise data platform and risk platform from the organisation file; the actual tools are not public.
